# HyperFrames Composition Project

## Skills — USE THESE FIRST

**Always invoke the relevant skill before writing or modifying compositions.** Skills encode framework-specific patterns (e.g., `window.__timelines` registration, `data-*` attribute semantics, shader-compatible CSS rules) that are NOT in generic web docs. Skipping them produces broken compositions.

**Doing anything with HyperFrames?** Start at `/hyperframes` — it tells you what HyperFrames can do and which skill or workflow handles your intent (make a video, TTS / BGM, prep footage, author / animate, render, install blocks), confirms your brief up front (the intent layer), and routes every "make me a…" request (a video, a deck, a composition port) to the right workflow. Read it first, especially when there's no project context to orient you. The workflows it routes to:

- `/product-launch-video` — any **website** URL or brief / script → a product launch / SaaS / promo video, or a site tour / showcase featuring the site's own captured visuals.
- `/faceless-explainer` — arbitrary text (topic / article / notes), **no URL, no website capture** → 60-90s faceless explainer.
- `/embedded-captions` — an existing talking-head video (MP4) → the same footage with captions / subtitles added (rail + embed, or pure-cinematic embed); the footage itself is untouched.
- `/talking-head-recut` — an existing talking-head / interview / podcast video (MP4) → the same footage **packaged with designed graphic overlays** (kinetic titles, lower-thirds, data callouts, pull-quotes, side panels, pip) synced to the transcript; the clip plays unchanged underneath. (Plain captions/subtitles → `/embedded-captions`.)
- `/pr-to-video` — a GitHub PR (URL / `owner/repo#N` / "this PR") → 30-90s code-change explainer (changelog / feature reveal / fix / refactor).
- `/motion-graphics` — a short (typically under 10s) design-led **motion graphic**, motion-is-the-message, no narration: kinetic type, a stat / number count-up, a chart, a logo sting, a lower-third / overlay, or an animated tweet / headline / captured-page highlight; rendered to MP4 or a transparent overlay. Longer / narrated / custom → `/general-video`.
- `/music-to-video` — a **music track** (audio file, video to pull audio from, or one generated from a mood brief) → beat-synced video (lyric / slideshow / kinetic promo). Music drives pacing; user-supplied images / videos are cut onto the same beat grid.
- `/slideshow` — a **presentation / pitch deck / interactive deck** — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered video.
- `/general-video` — fallback for any other video (title card, longer brand / sizzle reel, multi-scene montage, static loop, custom composition) and the home of **companion mode** — co-create with the full HyperFrames toolbox; the original hyperframes authoring flow, any length.

**Porting an existing composition?** `/remotion-to-hyperframes` translates a Remotion (React) composition into HyperFrames HTML — a source migration, separate from the creation workflows above.

The domain skills (`/hyperframes-core`, `/hyperframes-animation`, `/hyperframes-keyframes`, `/hyperframes-creative`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/media-use`, `/hyperframes-audio`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/figma`) and the full capability map live inside `/hyperframes` — it is the single source of truth for which skill handles which intent.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `/hyperframes-core` → `references/tailwind.md`.

> **Using a HyperFrames plugin?** Load skills from that installed bundle and follow
> its `hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md` execution rules. Update via
> the plugin manager, not the standalone commands below.
>
> **Standalone skill missing or stale?** Run `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` to install/refresh
> the specific skill you need (the `/hyperframes` router does this automatically before
> entering a workflow), or bare `npx hyperframes skills update` to refresh the core set plus
> everything already installed — neither pulls the full set. Restart the agent session so
> newly installed skills load.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # human-operated foreground preview (blocks until stopped)
npx hyperframes preview --background  # agent-safe persistent Studio preview
npx hyperframes preview --status      # verify the persistent preview is listening
npx hyperframes preview --stop        # stop it when review is finished
npm run check        # lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast (one command)
npm run render       # render to MP4
npm run publish      # publish and get a shareable link
npx hyperframes lint --verbose  # include info-level findings
npx hyperframes lint --json     # machine-readable output for CI
npx hyperframes docs <topic> # reference docs in terminal
```

> **Agents must use `npx hyperframes preview --background` for Studio handoff.** Do not rely
> on a shell/tool `run_in_background` wrapper around `npm run dev`: that foreground process
> remains owned by the invoking session and can disappear while the browser stays open,
> leaving refreshes at `ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`. Verify with `preview --status`, keep it
> alive through review, and stop it explicitly with `preview --stop` afterward.

> **Pinned CLI version.** These scripts pin an exact `hyperframes@X.Y.Z` so this project re-renders identically over time. Weeks later that pin lags fixes shipped since. To move up: `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check` (shows the delta), then `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .` to rewrite the pins. Always unpinned — the pinned script re-runs the old version against itself.

## Documentation

**For quick reference**, use the local CLI docs command (no network required):

```bash
npx hyperframes docs <topic>
```

Topics: `data-attributes`, `gsap`, `compositions`, `rendering`, `examples`, `troubleshooting`

**For full documentation**, discover pages via the machine-readable index — do NOT guess URLs:

```
https://hyperframes.heygen.com/llms.txt
```

## Project Structure

- `index.html` — main composition (root timeline)
- `compositions/` — sub-compositions referenced via `data-composition-src`
- `meta.json` — project metadata (id, name)
- `transcript.json` — whisper word-level transcript (if generated)

## Linting — ALWAYS RUN AFTER CHANGES

After creating or editing any `.html` composition, **always** run the full check before considering the task complete:

```bash
npm run check
```

Fix all errors before presenting the result. Warnings should be reviewed before rendering.

## Key Rules

1. Every timed element needs `data-start` and a duration. `data-start` is what marks it as timed; `data-track-index` is an optional Studio display lane the render never reads
2. Give timed visual elements `class="clip"`. The framework keys visibility off `data-start`, not the class, but the shared `.clip` CSS is what gives a scene its full-frame box, and `lint` warns without it
3. Register one paused root timeline per composition on `window.__timelines`:
   ```js
   window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
   window.__timelines["composition-id"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
   ```
   Scene timelines manually added to this root must not be paused. A paused
   child does not advance when the root is seeked. The runtime activates
   registered composition siblings, not arbitrary nested scene timelines.
4. Videos use `muted` with a separate `<audio>` element for the audio track
5. Sub-compositions use `data-composition-src="compositions/file.html"` to reference other HTML files
6. Only deterministic logic — no `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no network fetches

# HyperFrames Composition Project

## Skills — USE THESE FIRST

**Always invoke the relevant skill before writing or modifying compositions.** Skills encode framework-specific patterns (e.g., `window.__timelines` registration, `data-*` attribute semantics, shader-compatible CSS rules) that are NOT in generic web docs. Skipping them produces broken compositions.

**Doing anything with HyperFrames?** Start at `/hyperframes` — it tells you what HyperFrames can do and which skill or workflow handles your intent (make a video, TTS / BGM, prep footage, author / animate, render, install blocks), confirms your brief up front (the intent layer), and routes every "make me a…" request (a video, a deck, a composition port) to the right workflow. Read it first, especially when there's no project context to orient you. The workflows it routes to:

- `/product-launch-video` — any **website** URL or brief / script → a product launch / SaaS / promo video, or a site tour / showcase featuring the site's own captured visuals.
- `/faceless-explainer` — arbitrary text (topic / article / notes), **no URL, no website capture** → 60-90s faceless explainer.
- `/embedded-captions` — an existing talking-head video (MP4) → the same footage with captions / subtitles added (rail + embed, or pure-cinematic embed); the footage itself is untouched.
- `/talking-head-recut` — an existing talking-head / interview / podcast video (MP4) → the same footage **packaged with designed graphic overlays** (kinetic titles, lower-thirds, data callouts, pull-quotes, side panels, pip) synced to the transcript; the clip plays unchanged underneath. (Plain captions/subtitles → `/embedded-captions`.)
- `/pr-to-video` — a GitHub PR (URL / `owner/repo#N` / "this PR") → 30-90s code-change explainer (changelog / feature reveal / fix / refactor).
- `/motion-graphics` — a short (typically under 10s) design-led **motion graphic**, motion-is-the-message, no narration: kinetic type, a stat / number count-up, a chart, a logo sting, a lower-third / overlay, or an animated tweet / headline / captured-page highlight; rendered to MP4 or a transparent overlay. Longer / narrated / custom → `/general-video`.
- `/music-to-video` — a **music track** (audio file, video to pull audio from, or one generated from a mood brief) → beat-synced video (lyric / slideshow / kinetic promo). Music drives pacing; user-supplied images / videos are cut onto the same beat grid.
- `/slideshow` — a **presentation / pitch deck / interactive deck** — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered video.
- `/general-video` — fallback for any other video (title card, longer brand / sizzle reel, multi-scene montage, static loop, custom composition) and the home of **companion mode** — co-create with the full HyperFrames toolbox; the original hyperframes authoring flow, any length.

**Porting an existing composition?** `/remotion-to-hyperframes` translates a Remotion (React) composition into HyperFrames HTML — a source migration, separate from the creation workflows above.

The domain skills (`/hyperframes-core`, `/hyperframes-animation`, `/hyperframes-keyframes`, `/hyperframes-creative`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/media-use`, `/hyperframes-audio`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/figma`) and the full capability map live inside `/hyperframes` — it is the single source of truth for which skill handles which intent.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `/hyperframes-core` → `references/tailwind.md`.

> **Using a HyperFrames plugin?** Load skills from that installed bundle and follow
> its `hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md` execution rules. Update via
> the plugin manager, not the standalone commands below.
>
> **Standalone skill missing or stale?** Run `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` to install/refresh
> the specific skill you need (the `/hyperframes` router does this automatically before
> entering a workflow), or bare `npx hyperframes skills update` to refresh the core set plus
> everything already installed — neither pulls the full set. Restart the agent session so
> newly installed skills load.

- `/product-launch-video` — any **website** URL or brief / script → a product launch / SaaS / promo video, or a site tour / showcase featuring the site's own captured visuals.
- `/faceless-explainer` — arbitrary text (topic / article / notes), **no URL, no website capture** → 60-90s faceless explainer.
- `/embedded-captions` — an existing talking-head video (MP4) → the same footage with captions / subtitles added (rail + embed, or pure-cinematic embed); the footage itself is untouched.
- `/talking-head-recut` — an existing talking-head / interview / podcast video (MP4) → the same footage **packaged with designed graphic overlays** (kinetic titles, lower-thirds, data callouts, pull-quotes, side panels, pip) synced to the transcript; the clip plays unchanged underneath. (Plain captions/subtitles → `/embedded-captions`.)
- `/pr-to-video` — a GitHub PR (URL / `owner/repo#N` / "this PR") → 30-90s code-change explainer (changelog / feature reveal / fix / refactor).
- `/motion-graphics` — a short (typically under 10s) design-led **motion graphic**, motion-is-the-message, no narration: kinetic type, a stat / number count-up, a chart, a logo sting, a lower-third / overlay, or an animated tweet / headline / captured-page highlight; rendered to MP4 or a transparent overlay. Longer / narrated / custom → `/general-video`.
- `/music-to-video` — a **music track** (audio file, video to pull audio from, or one generated from a mood brief) → beat-synced video (lyric / slideshow / kinetic promo). Music drives pacing; user-supplied images / videos are cut onto the same beat grid.
- `/slideshow` — a **presentation / pitch deck / interactive deck** — discrete slides, fragment reveals, branching, hotspot navigation, presenter mode. Output is a navigable deck, not a rendered video.
- `/general-video` — fallback for any other video (title card, longer brand / sizzle reel, multi-scene montage, static loop, custom composition) and the home of **companion mode** — co-create with the full HyperFrames toolbox; the original hyperframes authoring flow, any length.

**Porting an existing composition?** `/remotion-to-hyperframes` translates a Remotion (React) composition into HyperFrames HTML — a source migration, separate from the creation workflows above.

The domain skills (`/hyperframes-core`, `/hyperframes-animation`, `/hyperframes-keyframes`, `/hyperframes-creative`, `/hyperframes-cli`, `/media-use`, `/hyperframes-audio`, `/hyperframes-registry`, `/figma`) and the full capability map live inside `/hyperframes` — it is the single source of truth for which skill handles which intent.

**Changing how real footage or images look or reveal?** Load `/media-use` and read its `references/media-treatments.md` before editing, even when the request only says dark, flat, boring, retro, private, or “make the reveal cooler.” It governs how footage is treated, never whether media may be used. Use canonical media treatments and seek-safe motion; do not improvise equivalent CSS/SVG filters or overlays.

> **Tailwind v4 projects** (`hyperframes init --tailwind`): see `/hyperframes-core` → `references/tailwind.md`.

> **Using a HyperFrames plugin?** Load skills from that installed bundle and follow
> its `hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md` execution rules. Update via
> the plugin manager, not the standalone commands below.
>
> **Standalone skill missing or stale?** Run `npx hyperframes skills update <name>` to install/refresh
> the specific skill you need (the `/hyperframes` router does this automatically before
> entering a workflow), or bare `npx hyperframes skills update` to refresh the core set plus
> everything already installed — neither pulls the full set. Restart the agent session so
> newly installed skills load.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev          # human-operated foreground preview (blocks until stopped)
npx hyperframes preview --background  # agent-safe persistent Studio preview
npx hyperframes preview --status      # verify the persistent preview is listening
npx hyperframes preview --stop        # stop it when review is finished
npm run check        # lint + runtime + layout + motion + contrast (one command)
npm run render       # render to MP4
npm run publish      # publish and get a shareable link
npx hyperframes lint --verbose  # include info-level findings
npx hyperframes lint --json     # machine-readable output for CI
npx hyperframes docs <topic> # reference docs in terminal
```

> **Agents must use `npx hyperframes preview --background` for Studio handoff.** Do not rely
> on a shell/tool `run_in_background` wrapper around `npm run dev`: that foreground process
> remains owned by the invoking session and can disappear while the browser stays open,
> leaving refreshes at `ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT`. Verify with `preview --status`, keep it
> alive through review, and stop it explicitly with `preview --stop` afterward.

> **Pinned CLI version.** These scripts pin an exact `hyperframes@X.Y.Z` so this project re-renders identically over time. Weeks later that pin lags fixes shipped since. To move up: `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project . --check` (shows the delta), then `npx hyperframes@latest upgrade --project .` to rewrite the pins. Always unpinned — the pinned script re-runs the old version against itself.

## Documentation

**For quick reference**, use the local CLI docs command (no network required):

```bash
npx hyperframes docs <topic>
```

Topics: `data-attributes`, `gsap`, `compositions`, `rendering`, `examples`, `troubleshooting`

**For full documentation**, discover pages via the machine-readable index — do NOT guess URLs:

```
https://hyperframes.heygen.com/llms.txt
```

## Project Structure

- `index.html` — main composition (root timeline)
- `compositions/` — sub-compositions referenced via `data-composition-src`
- `meta.json` — project metadata (id, name)
- `transcript.json` — whisper word-level transcript (if generated)

## Linting — ALWAYS RUN AFTER CHANGES

After creating or editing any `.html` composition, **always** run the full check before considering the task complete:

```bash
npm run check
```

Fix all errors before presenting the result. Warnings should be reviewed before rendering.

## Key Rules

1. Every timed element needs `data-start` and a duration. `data-start` is what marks it as timed; `data-track-index` is an optional Studio display lane the render never reads
2. Give timed visual elements `class="clip"`. The framework keys visibility off `data-start`, not the class, but the shared `.clip` CSS is what gives a scene its full-frame box, and `lint` warns without it
3. Register one paused root timeline per composition on `window.__timelines`:
   ```js
   window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
   window.__timelines["composition-id"] = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
   ```
   Scene timelines manually added to this root must not be paused. A paused
   child does not advance when the root is seeked. The runtime activates
   registered composition siblings, not arbitrary nested scene timelines.
4. Videos use `muted` with a separate `<audio>` element for the audio track
5. Sub-compositions use `data-composition-src="compositions/file.html"` to reference other HTML files
6. Only deterministic logic — no `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no network fetches

### priorities/audio/make_audio.py  (3,169 octets)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Subtle synthesized sound design (no music, no samples) for the priorities edit. Voice is the original track."""
import json, numpy as np
from scipy import signal
from scipy.io import wavfile
SR=44100; DUR=37.12; N=int(SR*DUR); rng=np.random.default_rng(3)
def lp(x,fc): b,a=signal.butter(2,fc/(SR/2),'low'); return signal.lfilter(b,a,x)
def hp(x,fc): b,a=signal.butter(2,fc/(SR/2),'high'); return signal.lfilter(b,a,x)
def env(n,tau): return np.exp(-np.arange(n)/(SR*tau))
def put(buf,t,x,g=1.0):
    i=int(max(0,t)*SR)
    if i>=buf.shape[-1]: return
    j=min(buf.shape[-1],i+len(x)); buf[i:j]+=x[:j-i]*g
def midi(m): return 440*2**((m-69)/12)
def whoosh(dur=0.55):
    n=int(dur*SR); t=np.arange(n)/SR; x=rng.standard_normal(n); y=np.zeros(n); blk=512
    fc=300+6000*(np.sin(np.pi*t/dur))**1.5
    for i in range(0,n,blk):
        f=float(fc[min(i,n-1)]); b,a=signal.butter(2,[f*0.5/(SR/2),min(f*1.7,14000)/(SR/2)],'band')
        seg=signal.lfilter(b,a,x[i:i+blk*2])[:blk]; y[i:i+len(seg)]=seg[:n-i]
    return y*np.sin(np.pi*t/dur)**1.2*0.5
def pop(f0=600):
    n=int(0.16*SR); t=np.arange(n)/SR; f=f0+500*np.exp(-t*38); ph=2*np.pi*np.cumsum(f)/SR
    return np.sin(ph)*env(n,0.05)*0.5
def tick():
    n=int(0.05*SR); return (hp(rng.standard_normal(n),2500)*env(n,0.008)*0.35)
def slash():
    n=int(0.28*SR); t=np.arange(n)/SR; x=hp(rng.standard_normal(n),1800)*np.minimum(1,t/0.01)*np.exp(-t*9)*0.35
    return x+np.sin(2*np.pi*(900-1100*t)*t)*env(n,0.08)*0.12
def clash():
    n=int(1.0*SR); t=np.arange(n)/SR; f=60+80*np.exp(-t*18); ph=2*np.pi*np.cumsum(f)/SR
    return np.sin(ph)*env(n,0.16)*0.7+lp(rng.standard_normal(n),3000)*env(n,0.12)*0.25
def win():
    out=np.zeros(int(2.2*SR))
    for k,m in enumerate([72,76,79,84]):
        n=int(1.6*SR); t=np.arange(n)/SR; f=midi(m)
        s=(np.sin(2*np.pi*f*t)+0.4*np.sin(2*np.pi*f*2.76*t)*env(n,0.3))*env(n,0.6)*0.3
        put(out,k*0.07,s)
    return out
def swish(dur=0.3,g=0.5):
    n=int(dur*SR); t=np.arange(n)/SR; x=rng.standard_normal(n); y=np.zeros(n); blk=512
    fc=800+5000*(t/dur)**1.3
    for i in range(0,n,blk):
        f=float(fc[min(i,n-1)]); b,a=signal.butter(2,[f*0.6/(SR/2),min(f*1.6,14000)/(SR/2)],'band')
        seg=signal.lfilter(b,a,x[i:i+blk*2])[:blk]; y[i:i+len(seg)]=seg[:n-i]
    return y*np.sin(np.pi*t/dur)**1.5*g
def thock(g=0.5):
    n=int(0.14*SR); t=np.arange(n)/SR; f=170-90*t/0.14; ph=2*np.pi*np.cumsum(f)/SR
    return (np.sin(ph)*env(n,0.045)+hp(rng.standard_normal(n),3000)*env(n,0.006)*0.3)*g
S=np.zeros(N)
for e in json.load(open('events.json')):
    k=e['k']; t=e['t']
    if k=='swish': put(S,t,swish(0.3,0.6),1.0)
    elif k=='swish2': put(S,t,swish(0.22,0.35),1.0)
    elif k=='thock': put(S,t,thock(0.6),1.0)
    elif k=='thock2': put(S,t,thock(0.3),1.0)
    elif k=='whoosh': put(S,t-0.2,whoosh(),1.0)
    elif k=='pop': put(S,t,pop(e.get('f',600)),0.9)
    elif k=='tick': put(S,t,tick(),0.8)
    elif k=='slash': put(S,t,slash(),1.0)
    elif k=='clash': put(S,t,clash(),0.6)
    elif k=='win': put(S,t,win(),1.0)
S*=0.85/max(1e-9,np.abs(S).max())
wavfile.write('sfx.wav',SR,(np.clip(S,-1,1)*32767).astype(np.int16)); print('ok')

### priorities/audio/make_paper.py  (944 octets)

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import sys
for SUF,AMP,ANG in (('',1.0,-24),('2',2.1,-32)):
    W,H=1200,2100
    y,x=np.mgrid[0:H,0:W].astype(np.float32)
    base=0.93+0.04*(1-y/H)+0.02*(x/W)
    ang=np.deg2rad(ANG); u=x*np.cos(ang)+y*np.sin(ang)
    img=base.copy()
    for c,w,a in [(-300,160,.06),(150,120,.05),(520,200,.07),(900,90,.04),(1300,170,.06),(1700,130,.05)]:
        img+=a*np.exp(-((u-c)/w)**2)
    for c,w,a in [(-60,110,.07),(330,150,.08),(700,100,.06),(1090,160,.08),(1500,90,.05)]:
        img-=AMP*a*np.exp(-((u-c)/w)**2)
    # soft vignette
    r=np.sqrt(((x-W/2)/(W/2))**2+((y-H/2)/(H/2))**2); img-=0.035*r**2
    rng=np.random.default_rng(5); img+=rng.normal(0,0.012,(H,W)).astype(np.float32)
    img=np.clip(img,0,1)
    rgb=np.stack([img*0.985+0.0,img*0.985,img*0.975],-1)
    Image.fromarray((rgb*255).astype(np.uint8)).save('/home/user/priorities/app/assets/paper%s.jpg'%SUF,quality=88)
    print('ok')

### leger-video/music/make_music.py  (12,106 octets)
==============================================================================
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Original 60 s soundtrack for the Léger Akodjenou film — 100 % synthesized (no samples, no licensing).
120 BPM (beat = 0.5 s) so every scene cut / reveal in the video lands on a beat.
Key: F minor. Dark, confident, "premium tech" pulse with ember-warm pad."""
import numpy as np
from scipy import signal
from scipy.io import wavfile

SR = 44100
DUR = 60.0
N = int(SR * DUR)
BEAT = 0.5
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)  # seeded -> deterministic

L = np.zeros(N); R = np.zeros(N)
REV_L = np.zeros(N); REV_R = np.zeros(N)  # reverb send bus
KICK_ENV = np.zeros(N)  # for side-chain


def put(buf, t, x, gain=1.0):
    i = int(t * SR)
    if i >= N or i < 0:
        return
    j = min(N, i + len(x))
    buf[i:j] += x[: j - i] * gain


def stereo(x, t, g=1.0, pan=0.0, send=0.0):
    gl = g * np.cos((pan + 1) * np.pi / 4)
    gr = g * np.sin((pan + 1) * np.pi / 4)
    put(L, t, x, gl); put(R, t, x, gr)
    if send:
        put(REV_L, t, x, gl * send); put(REV_R, t, x, gr * send)


def env_exp(n, tau):
    return np.exp(-np.arange(n) / (SR * tau))


def lp(x, fc, order=2):
    b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), 'low'); return signal.lfilter(b, a, x)


def hp(x, fc, order=2):
    b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), 'high'); return signal.lfilter(b, a, x)


def midi(n):
    return 440.0 * 2 ** ((n - 69) / 12)


# ---------- instruments ----------
def kick():
    n = int(SR * 0.45); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 48 + 120 * np.exp(-t * 28)
    ph = 2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR
    x = np.sin(ph) * np.exp(-t * 7.5)
    click = hp(rng.standard_normal(n), 2500) * np.exp(-t * 350) * 0.25
    return np.tanh((x + click) * 1.6) * 0.95


def clap():
    n = int(SR * 0.4); x = np.zeros(n)
    for d in (0, 0.011, 0.022):
        k = int(d * SR)
        m = n - k
        x[k:] += hp(lp(rng.standard_normal(m), 7500), 900) * np.exp(-np.arange(m) / (SR * 0.02))
    tail = hp(lp(rng.standard_normal(n), 6000), 1000) * np.exp(-np.arange(n) / (SR * 0.11))
    return (x * 0.6 + tail * 0.5) * 0.7


def hat(open_=False):
    n = int(SR * (0.22 if open_ else 0.06))
    x = hp(rng.standard_normal(n), 7000, 3) * env_exp(n, 0.07 if open_ else 0.015)
    return x * 0.35


def sub_note(f, dur):
    n = int(SR * dur); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) + 0.25 * np.sin(4 * np.pi * f * t)
    a = np.minimum(1, t / 0.006) * np.minimum(1, (dur - t) / 0.04)
    return np.tanh(x * 1.3) * a * 0.55


def pluck(f, dur=0.35):
    n = int(SR * dur); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = signal.sawtooth(2 * np.pi * f * t) * 0.5 + signal.square(2 * np.pi * f * 1.004 * t, 0.4) * 0.3
    cutoff = 600 + 5200 * np.exp(-t * 14)
    # time-varying lowpass via block processing
    out = np.zeros(n); zi = None; blk = 256
    for s in range(0, n, blk):
        b, a = signal.butter(2, min(cutoff[s], 12000) / (SR / 2), 'low')
        if zi is None:
            zi = signal.lfilter_zi(b, a) * x[s]
        y, zi = signal.lfilter(b, a, x[s:s + blk], zi=zi)
        out[s:s + blk] = y
    return out * np.exp(-t * 9) * 0.5


def pad_chord(notes, dur):
    n = int(SR * (dur + 1.2)); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = np.zeros(n)
    for m in notes:
        for det in (-0.07, 0.0, 0.07):
            f = midi(m + det)
            x += signal.sawtooth(2 * np.pi * f * t + rng.uniform(0, 6.28))
    x /= (len(notes) * 3)
    x = lp(x, 1500, 2)
    a = np.minimum(1, t / 1.6) * np.where(t < dur, 1, np.exp(-(t - dur) * 3.2))
    return x * a * 0.55


def impact(dur=3.0, boom=True):
    n = int(SR * dur); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = np.zeros(n)
    if boom:
        f = 38 + 90 * np.exp(-t * 6)
        x += np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR) * np.exp(-t * 1.6) * 0.95
    nz = rng.standard_normal(n)
    x += hp(lp(nz, 9000), 400) * np.exp(-t * 2.6) * 0.38
    return np.tanh(x * 1.2)


def riser(dur):
    n = int(SR * dur); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    nz = rng.standard_normal(n)
    out = np.zeros(n); blk = 512; zi = None
    for s in range(0, n, blk):
        fc = 300 + 9000 * (s / n) ** 2
        b, a = signal.butter(2, min(fc, 14000) / (SR / 2), 'high')
        if zi is None:
            zi = signal.lfilter_zi(b, a) * 0
        y, zi = signal.lfilter(b, a, nz[s:s + blk], zi=zi)
        out[s:s + blk] = y
    amp = (t / dur) ** 2.2
    # tonal sweep
    f = 200 * 2 ** (3.2 * t / dur)
    tone = np.sin(2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR) * 0.18
    return (out * 0.35 + tone) * amp


def whoosh(dur=0.5, up=True):
    n = int(SR * dur); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    nz = rng.standard_normal(n)
    out = np.zeros(n); blk = 256; zi = None
    for s in range(0, n, blk):
        p = s / n
        fc = 500 + 7000 * (p if up else 1 - p)
        b, a = signal.butter(2, [max(200, fc * 0.5) / (SR / 2), min(fc * 1.5, 18000) / (SR / 2)], 'band')
        if zi is None:
            zi = signal.lfilter_zi(b, a) * 0
        y, zi = signal.lfilter(b, a, nz[s:s + blk], zi=zi)
        out[s:s + blk] = y
    a = np.sin(np.pi * t / dur) ** 2
    return out * a * 0.9


def tick(freq=1760, dur=0.22):
    n = int(SR * dur); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * t) + 0.4 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * 2.01 * t)
    return x * np.exp(-t * 22) * 0.35


def stat_hit(freq=880):
    n = int(SR * 0.7); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * t) * np.exp(-t * 7) + 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * freq * 1.5 * t) * np.exp(-t * 9)
    sub = np.sin(2 * np.pi * 55 * t) * np.exp(-t * 9) * 0.8
    return (x * 0.35 + sub * 0.5)


# ---------- arrangement ----------
CH = [  # F minor progression, 4 bars (8 s) each
    ([53, 56, 60, 63], 41),   # Fm7        bass F1
    ([49, 56, 60, 65], 37),   # Db (add)   bass Db1
    ([56, 60, 63, 67], 44),   # Ab         bass Ab1
    ([51, 55, 58, 62], 39),   # Eb         bass Eb1
]


def chord_at(t):
    return CH[int(t // 8) % 4]


def section(t):
    """returns dict of active layers at time t"""
    return t


# sections (seconds): (start, end, layers)
SEC = [
    (0, 7,   dict(kick='sparse', hat=False, clap=False, bass=False, arp=False, pad=True)),
    (7, 13,  dict(kick='four', hat=True, clap=True, bass=True, arp=False, pad=True)),
    (13, 26, dict(kick='four', hat=True, clap=True, bass=True, arp=True, pad=True, drive=True)),
    (26, 40, dict(kick='four', hat=True, clap=True, bass=True, arp=True, pad=True)),
    (40, 46, dict(kick=None, hat=False, clap=False, bass=False, arp=True, pad=True, soft=True)),
    (46, 52, dict(kick='four', hat=True, clap=True, bass=True, arp=True, pad=True)),
    (52, 58, dict(kick='four', hat=True, clap=True, bass=True, arp=True, pad=True, drive=True)),
    (58, 60, dict(kick=None, hat=False, clap=False, bass=False, arp=False, pad=True)),
]

K = kick(); C = clap(); HC = hat(False); HO = hat(True)

# pads: one chord per 8 s, overlapping tails
for i in range(0, int(DUR // 8) + 1):
    notes, _ = CH[i % 4]
    p = pad_chord(notes, 8.0)
    stereo(p, i * 8.0, 0.55, 0.0, send=0.35)

# drone sub under the intro
for s, e, lay in SEC:
    pass

kick_times = []
for s, e, lay in SEC:
    t = s
    while t < e - 1e-6:
        beat_idx = round((t - s) / BEAT)
        if lay.get('kick') == 'four':
            kick_times.append(t)
        elif lay.get('kick') == 'sparse':
            if t >= 3.0 and abs((t % 2.0)) < 1e-6:
                kick_times.append(t)
            elif t >= 5.0 and abs((t % 2.0) - 1.0) < 1e-6:
                kick_times.append(t)
        t += BEAT
# the cut beats get a bigger kick via impacts; remove duplicate at exact impact times later
for t in kick_times:
    stereo(K, t, 0.95, 0.0)
    i = int(t * SR); KICK_ENV[i:i + int(SR * 0.28)] = np.maximum(KICK_ENV[i:i + int(SR * 0.28)], np.linspace(1, 0, int(SR * 0.28)) ** 0.6)

for s, e, lay in SEC:
    t = s
    while t < e - 1e-6:
        bi = int(round(t / BEAT))
        if lay.get('clap') and bi % 2 == 1:
            stereo(C, t, 0.5, 0.05, send=0.3)
        if lay.get('hat'):
            stereo(HC, t + BEAT / 2, 0.55, 0.25)           # off-beat open-ish hat
            if bi % 4 == 3:
                stereo(HO, t + BEAT / 2, 0.45, 0.3)
            if lay.get('drive') or (s >= 13 and e > 20):
                stereo(HC, t + BEAT / 4, 0.22, -0.2)
                stereo(HC, t + 3 * BEAT / 4, 0.28, 0.2)
        if lay.get('bass'):
            _, root = chord_at(t)
            f = midi(root)
            # off-beat 8th bass (side-chain feel): hits on the "and"
            stereo(sub_note(f, BEAT * 0.42), t + BEAT / 2, 0.62, 0.0)
            if lay.get('drive') and bi % 2 == 0:
                stereo(sub_note(f * 2, BEAT * 0.2), t + BEAT * 0.75, 0.3, 0.0)
        t += BEAT

# arp (16ths, pattern over chord tones) with ping-pong echo via reverb send
pat = [0, 2, 1, 3, 2, 1, 3, 2]
for s, e, lay in SEC:
    if not lay.get('arp'):
        continue
    step = BEAT / 2
    t = s; k = 0
    while t < e - 1e-6:
        notes, _ = chord_at(t)
        nn = notes[pat[k % len(pat)] % len(notes)] + 24
        g = 0.26 if lay.get('soft') else 0.2
        if lay.get('drive'):
            g = 0.28
        pk = pluck(midi(nn), 0.3)
        pan = -0.5 if k % 2 == 0 else 0.5
        stereo(pk, t, g, pan, send=0.4)
        # echo (dotted 8th)
        stereo(pk, t + BEAT * 0.75, g * 0.35, -pan, send=0.3)
        t += step; k += 1

# soft piano-ish melody for testimonial (40-46)
mel = [(40.0, 72), (41.0, 70), (42.0, 68), (43.0, 70), (44.0, 72), (45.0, 75)]
for t, m in mel:
    n = int(SR * 1.8); tt = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = (np.sin(2 * np.pi * midi(m) * tt) + 0.3 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * midi(m) * 2 * tt) + 0.1 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * midi(m) * 3 * tt)) * np.exp(-tt * 2.6)
    stereo(x * 0.28, t, 1.0, 0.1, send=0.6)

# ---------- FX / sync points ----------
cuts = [7, 13, 26, 33, 40, 46, 52]
for c in cuts:
    stereo(whoosh(0.55, up=True), c - 0.55, 0.55, 0.0, send=0.2)
    stereo(impact(2.4, boom=True), c, 0.6 if c != 52 else 0.95, 0.0, send=0.25)
    stereo(whoosh(0.8, up=False), c, 0.3, 0.0, send=0.2)

# opening slam
stereo(impact(3.4, boom=True), 0.0, 0.95, 0.0, send=0.3)
stereo(riser(2.0), 5.0, 0.55, 0.0, send=0.3)             # riser into scene 2
stereo(riser(1.5), 11.5, 0.4, 0.0, send=0.3)             # into services
stereo(riser(3.0), 49.0, 0.5, 0.0, send=0.3)             # into final
stereo(riser(2.0), 37.8, 0.3, 0.0, send=0.2)             # into testimonial

# ticks synced to visual reveals
ticks_hi = [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 7.5, 8.0, 11.0, 11.5, 12.0, 26.5, 27.25, 28.0, 28.75, 29.5, 30.25, 46.5, 47.5, 48.5]
for t in ticks_hi:
    stereo(tick(1568), t, 0.6, 0.0, send=0.3)
for i, t in enumerate([35.5, 36.0, 36.5, 37.0, 37.5, 38.0]):
    stereo(tick(1319 + 110 * i), t, 0.5, 0.0, send=0.3)
for i, t in enumerate([13.5, 16.0, 18.5, 21.0, 23.5]):
    stereo(stat_hit(698 * (1 + 0.06 * i)), t, 0.9, 0.0, send=0.3)
stereo(stat_hit(880), 40.5, 0.8, 0.0, send=0.3)
stereo(stat_hit(1175), 54.5, 0.7, 0.0, send=0.35)   # button pop
# final chord swell + tail
stereo(pad_chord([53, 60, 65, 68], 6.0), 54.0, 0.5, 0.0, send=0.5)

# ---------- reverb ----------
ir_n = int(SR * 2.4)
ir = rng.standard_normal(ir_n) * np.exp(-np.arange(ir_n) / (SR * 0.55))
ir = lp(ir, 5500) * 0.04
ir2 = rng.standard_normal(ir_n) * np.exp(-np.arange(ir_n) / (SR * 0.55)); ir2 = lp(ir2, 5500) * 0.04
wet_l = signal.fftconvolve(REV_L, ir)[:N]
wet_r = signal.fftconvolve(REV_R, ir2)[:N]
L += wet_l * 0.9; R += wet_r * 0.9

# ---------- side-chain ducking on pad/bass/arp-ish glue (simple global duck on non-kick) ----------
# apply to whole mix except kick: approximate by ducking the sum 18% on kick envelope after adding kick back
duck = 1 - 0.28 * KICK_ENV
L *= duck; R *= duck

# ---------- master ----------
# fade in/out
fi = np.minimum(1, np.arange(N) / (SR * 0.02))
fo = np.minimum(1, (N - np.arange(N)) / (SR * 2.0)) ** 1.5
L *= fi * fo; R *= fi * fo
mix = np.stack([L, R], 1)
mix = hp(mix.T, 28, 2).T
# gentle bus compression-ish via tanh
mix = np.tanh(mix * 1.15) / np.tanh(1.15)
peak = np.max(np.abs(mix))
mix = mix / peak * 0.89  # -1 dBFS
wavfile.write('music.wav', SR, (mix * 32767).astype(np.int16))
print('ok', mix.shape, 'peak', np.max(np.abs(mix)), 'rms', np.sqrt(np.mean(mix ** 2)))

      pjs.forEach((p, i) => {
        const t = 27.5 + i * 2.5;
        // enter
        T.fromTo(p, { yPercent: i === 0 ? 0 : 100, opacity: i === 0 ? 0 : 1 }, { yPercent: 0, opacity: 1, duration: 0.6, ease: "expo.out" }, t - (i === 0 ? 0 : 0.0));
        if (i < pjs.length - 1) T.to(p, { yPercent: -100, opacity: 0, duration: 0.5, ease: "power3.inOut" }, t + 2.5);
        // row highlight
        const r = rows[i];
        T.to(r.querySelector(".fill"), { scaleX: 1, duration: 0.35, ease: "power3.out" }, t);
        [".i", ".nm", ".ty"].forEach((s) => { const e = r.querySelector(s); if (e) T.to(e, { color: "#0a0a0b", duration: 0.2 }, t + 0.05); });
        if (i < pjs.length - 1) {
          T.to(r.querySelector(".fill"), { scaleX: 0, transformOrigin: "right center", duration: 0.35, ease: "power3.in" }, t + 2.5);
          T.to(r.querySelector(".i"), { color: "#ff4d00", duration: 0.2 }, t + 2.5);
          T.to(r.querySelector(".nm"), { color: "#f4f1ea", duration: 0.2 }, t + 2.5);
          if (r.querySelector(".ty")) T.to(r.querySelector(".ty"), { color: "#a29e94", duration: 0.2 }, t + 2.5);
        }
        // funnel level
        T.to(fns[i], { fill: "rgba(255,77,0,0.9)", stroke: "#ff4d00", duration: 0.35, ease: "power2.out" }, t + 0.1);
        // counter + staggered content
        counter(p.querySelector(".cnt"), tgt[i], t + 0.25, 1.2, { dec: dec[i], ease: "expo.out" });
        T.fromTo(p.querySelector(".big"), { scale: 0.86, transformOrigin: "left center" }, { scale: 1, duration: 0.8, ease: "back.out(1.6)" }, t + 0.2);
        T.fromTo(p.querySelector(".lab"), { opacity: 0, x: -40 }, { opacity: 1, x: 0, duration: 0.6, ease: "power3.out" }, t + 0.6);
        T.fromTo(p.querySelectorAll(".tags .pill"), { opacity: 0, y: 24 }, { opacity: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.45, ease: "power2.out", stagger: 0.1 }, t + 0.75);
        T.fromTo(p.querySelector(".top"), { opacity: 0, y: -24 }, { opacity: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.55, ease: "power3.out" }, t + 0.15);
      });
      // after the last item the stat holds; slight push for life
      T.to("#s5stage", { scale: 1.012, duration: 12, ease: "sine.inOut" }, 27.9);

      /* ================= S6 · TÉMOIGNAGE (40–46) ================= */
      OFF = 0;
      T.fromTo("#s6b", { opacity: 0, x: -60 }, { opacity: 1, x: 0, duration: 0.7, ease: "power3.out" }, 40.35);
      counter($("#s6n1"), 9, 40.4, 0.6, { ease: "power2.out" });
      T.fromTo("#s6arr", { scaleX: 0, opacity: 0 }, { scaleX: 1, opacity: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "power4.out" }, 40.9);
      T.fromTo("#s6a", { opacity: 0, scale: 0.6, transformOrigin: "left center" }, { opacity: 1, scale: 1, duration: 0.7, ease: "back.out(1.7)" }, 41.1);
      counter($("#s6n2"), 23, 41.15, 1.2, { ease: "expo.out" });
      T.fromTo("#s6cap", { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 1, duration: 0.6 }, 41.5);
      T.fromTo("#s6q", { opacity: 0, y: 40, filter: "blur(10px)" }, { opacity: 1, y: 0, filter: "blur(0px)", duration: 0.9, ease: "power3.out" }, 42.2);
      T.fromTo("#s6who", { opacity: 0, x: -40 }, { opacity: 1, x: 0, duration: 0.6, ease: "power3.out" }, 43.6);
      T.fromTo("#s6ba", { scale: 1, transformOrigin: "left center" }, { scale: 1.04, duration: 5.5, ease: "sine.inOut" }, 40.4);

      /* ================= S7 · OFFRE (46–52) ================= */
      T.fromTo("#s7h1", { yPercent: 115 }, { yPercent: 0, duration: 0.9, ease: "expo.out" }, 46.3);
      ["#g1", "#g2", "#g3"].forEach((g, i) => {
        const t = 46.5 + i;
        T.fromTo(g, { opacity: 0, x: -120 }, { opacity: 1, x: 0, duration: 0.7, ease: "expo.out" }, t - 0.1);
        T.to(g + " .ck path", { strokeDashoffset: 0, duration: 0.45, ease: "power2.out" }, t + 0.2);
        T.fromTo(g + " .ck", { scale: 0.4 }, { scale: 1, duration: 0.5, ease: "back.out(2.2)" }, t + 0.05);
      });
      T.fromTo("#s7d", { opacity: 0, x: V ? 0 : 100, y: V ? 80 : 0 }, { opacity: 1, x: 0, y: 0, duration: 0.9, ease: "expo.out" }, 46.8);
      counter($("#d1"), 5, 47.4, 0.9);
      T.to("#b1", { scaleX: 1, duration: 1.0, ease: "power3.out" }, 47.6);
      T.to("#b2", { scaleX: 1, duration: 1.3, ease: "power3.out" }, 48.0);

      /* ================= S8 · CTA (52–60) ================= */

      T.fromTo("#s8h2", { yPercent: 115 }, { yPercent: 0, duration: 0.95, ease: "expo.out" }, 52.9);

### rockwood-edit/audio/build_v1.py  (4,016 octets)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Builds app/index.html — Rockwood Method talking-head edit (9:16, 1080x1920, 27.6 s).
Captions are generated from the word-level transcript (audio/words.json)."""
import json, re, html

DUR = 27.6
words = json.load(open("/home/user/rockwood-edit/audio/words.json"))

# ───────── normalise tokens (merge ASR fragments, drop trailing punctuation) ─────────
toks = []
i = 0
while i < len(words):
    w = dict(words[i]); t = w["text"]
    if t.lower() == "self" and i + 1 < len(words) and words[i + 1]["text"].startswith("-"):
        n = words[i + 1]; w = {"text": "self" + n["text"], "start": w["start"], "end": n["end"]}; i += 1
    elif t == "100" and i + 1 < len(words) and words[i + 1]["text"] == "%":
        n = words[i + 1]; w = {"text": "100%", "start": w["start"], "end": n["end"]}; i += 1
    elif t.lower() == "rockwoodmethod" and i + 1 < len(words) and words[i + 1]["text"].startswith("."):
        n = words[i + 1]; w = {"text": "rockwoodmethod.com", "start": w["start"], "end": n["end"]}; i += 1
    elif t.lower().startswith("shop") and toks and toks[-1]["text"] == "rockwoodmethod.com":
        w = {"text": "/shop", "start": w["start"], "end": w["end"]}
    w["text"] = re.sub(r"[.,!?;:]+$", "", w["text"])
    toks.append(w); i += 1

CHUNKS = [
    (0, 2), (3, 5), (6, 8), (9, 10), (11, 13), (14, 15), (16, 17), (18, 18), (19, 21), (22, 25), (26, 28),
    (29, 32), (33, 36), (37, 40), (41, 42), (43, 46), (47, 48), (49, 50), (51, 53), (54, 55), (56, 57),
    (58, 61), (62, 63), (64, 67),
]
KW = {"wall", "street", "bros", "potato", "magic", "game", "changer", "rock", "solid", "hassle", "savings", "stress", "100%", "self-guided"}
assert CHUNKS[-1][1] == len(toks) - 1, (CHUNKS[-1], len(toks))

cap_html, cap_js = [], []
for ci, (a, b) in enumerate(CHUNKS):
    st = max(0.0, toks[a]["start"] - 0.05)
    nxt = toks[CHUNKS[ci + 1][0]]["start"] - 0.05 if ci + 1 < len(CHUNKS) else DUR
    en = min(nxt, toks[b]["end"] + 0.45)
    if ci + 1 == len(CHUNKS): en = min(DUR, toks[b]["end"] + 0.5)
    spans = []
    long = any(len(toks[k]["text"]) > 14 for k in range(a, b + 1))
    for k in range(a, b + 1):
        cls = "w kw" if toks[k]["text"].lower() in KW else "w"
        spans.append(f'<span class="{cls}" data-layout-allow-overlap id="w{k}">{html.escape(toks[k]["text"])}</span>')
    cap_html.append(
        f'<div class="clip cap{" sm" if long else ""}" data-layout-allow-overlap id="c{ci}" data-start="{st:.3f}" data-duration="{en - st:.3f}" data-track-index="1">'
        f'<div class="capin" id="ci{ci}">{" ".join(spans)}</div></div>')
    cap_js.append(f'capIn({ci}, {st:.3f});')
    for k in range(a, b + 1):
        e2 = toks[k + 1]["start"] if k < b else toks[k]["end"] + 0.1
        cap_js.append(f'hl({k}, {toks[k]["start"]:.3f}, {e2:.3f});')

# ───────── camera plan (scale punch-ins at the silent gaps between sentences) ─────────
CAM = [  # (start, end, scale_from, scale_to)
    (0.00, 2.30, 1.000, 1.045),
    (2.30, 4.06, 1.090, 1.125),
    (4.06, 8.02, 1.000, 1.025),
    (8.02, 12.53, 1.060, 1.085),
    (12.53, 13.54, 1.090, 1.120),
    (13.54, 17.06, 1.000, 1.040),
    (17.06, 19.58, 1.065, 1.090),
    (19.58, 22.50, 1.000, 1.040),
    (22.50, DUR, 1.060, 1.095),
]
cam_js = "\n".join(
    f'tl.set("#cam", {{ scale: {a_:.3f} }}, {s:.3f}); tl.to("#cam", {{ scale: {b_:.3f}, duration: {e - s:.3f}, ease: "sine.inOut" }}, {s:.3f});'
    for s, e, a_, b_ in CAM)

TPL = open("/home/user/rockwood-edit/template.html").read()
out = (TPL.replace("/*__CAPS_HTML__*/", "\n      ".join(cap_html))
          .replace("/*__CAPS_JS__*/", "\n      ".join(cap_js))
          .replace("/*__CAM_JS__*/", cam_js)
          .replace("/*__MUSIC_TAG__*/", open("/home/user/rockwood-edit/audio/music_tag.html").read())
          .replace("__DUR__", str(DUR)))
open("/home/user/rockwood-edit/app/index.html", "w").write(out)
print("built", len(toks), "tokens,", len(CHUNKS), "caption chunks")

### .agents/skills/media-use/SKILL.md  (8,188 octets)
==============================================================================
---
name: media-use
description: Agent Media OS, the single skill for every media need in a HyperFrames project. Resolve BGM, SFX, image, icon, brand logo, voice, color grade, or LUT into a frozen local file or paste-ready block + ledger record (one verb, `resolve`); generate via TTS / music / image models when the catalog misses; produce voiceover, transcription, captions, and background removal through one shared audio engine; operate on media (cut / reframe / transform); and reuse assets across projects. Also use for vague feedback that real footage looks dark, flat, boring, should feel retro/camcorder/print/ASCII, needs privacy, or needs a media reveal.
---

**Plugin installs:** Before setup or freshness commands, follow [plugin execution rules](../hyperframes/references/plugin-installation.md) when this skill is inside a HyperFrames plugin. Standalone installs keep the update instructions below.

# media-use

The media OS for HyperFrames: resolve · generate · operate · remember — every media type, one skill, zero context noise.

First run: install and sign in to the `heygen` CLI (the free-usage path), then verify with `npx hyperframes media-use resolve --doctor`. Setup and providers: `references/setup-providers.md`.

## Resolve — the one verb

```bash
npx hyperframes media-use resolve --type <type> --intent "<description>" --project <dir>
```

Returns one line: `resolved <id> → <path> (<type>, <metadata>)`. All search noise stays on disk.

| Type    | One-line intent                                                                  |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bgm`   | background music (HeyGen catalog, 10k+ tracks)                                   |
| `sfx`   | sound effects (bundled 19-file library + catalog)                                |
| `image` | photos, backgrounds (HeyGen asset search, 75k+ vectors)                          |
| `icon`  | icons, symbols (transparent)                                                     |
| `logo`  | official brand marks (theSVG → GitHub avatar → favicon; never redrawn)           |
| `voice` | TTS voiceover (HeyGen free-usage path; optional local Kokoro)                    |
| `grade` | measured correction candidate; broad polish/stylization follows Media Treatments |
| `lut`   | user-provided or explicitly chosen reusable validated `.cube` file               |

Before resolving fresh, list reusable candidates with `--candidates` and judge fit yourself — reuse rules, all flags, ingest (`--from`), and adopt are in `references/resolve.md`.

## Treat broad visual feedback as media intent

When a user explicitly asks to fix, polish, stylize, obscure, emphasize, or
reveal photographic media, read `references/media-treatments.md` even if they
do not name color grading or an effect. Inspect the real `<img>`/`<video>`,
choose one primary intent, then use deterministic persistence and verification.
Use a matching recipe as an optional tested seed, or inspect
`hyperframes media-treatment --capabilities --json`, then request one relevant
family/effect with `--capability <id>` and assemble a custom treatment from
canonical controls. Never load `--all` for ordinary authoring. A treatment may
compose correction, a preset, finishing, compatible shader effects, supported
keyframes, and optional Registry overlays. Add only source-justified bounded
tuning and compatible parts, never effects merely to make the result look more
sophisticated. Persist the final combined payload with
`hyperframes media-treatment`.

Use one progressively escalating workflow. For video, inspect one labeled
early/middle/late contact sheet rather than reading frames separately. Apply one
candidate and inspect one after-sheet for ordinary correction or polish.
Escalate to individual frames or moving draft evidence only when the result is
ambiguous, temporal, stylized, LUT-based, HDR/LOG-sensitive, private, or
brand-critical.

For ordinary correction or polish, persist the final treatment's
preset/adjustment JSON.
Do not generate a `.cube` LUT merely to encode exposure, shadows, contrast, or
warmth. Use a LUT only when the user supplies one or the selected treatment
explicitly owns one. `resolve --type grade --for ... --analyze` is measurement
evidence, not permission to replace the chosen treatment with a generated LUT.
Do not recreate supported vignette, grain, blur, pixelate, color, or treatment
effects with CSS/SVG overlays; that bypasses Studio controls and the canonical
preview/render shader path.

## Be proactive — run a media opportunity pass

The human usually can't tell which media would lift the piece. You can. When you build or review a composition, do **one** grounded scan and then **ask once** — don't silently add, and don't nag per asset.

Surface an opportunity only when a concrete signal is present:

| Signal detected                                          | Offer                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| On-screen text / a script with no voiceover              | TTS voiceover (audio engine)                                                                           |
| Emoji or a `<div>` styled as an icon                     | resolve real `icon`s                                                                                   |
| Image that is a placeholder, tiny, or upscaled-looking   | a better `image` (and/or upscale — see `references/operations.md`)                                     |
| Hard scene cuts / transitions with no sound              | transition `sfx`                                                                                       |
| A piece over ~10s with no music bed                      | `bgm`                                                                                                  |
| Footage that reads under/over-exposed or color-cast      | a corrective grade (inspect it with `hyperframes media-treatment --selector '#hero' --analyze --json`) |
| Photographic media that feels visually flat or off-topic | one specific source-appropriate preset or custom treatment, with the intended target named             |
| A meaningful media entrance/reveal that feels static     | one supported seek-safe treatment animation; preserve color unless the request also justifies a preset |

Rules that keep this a help, not nagware: **grounded, not generic** (no signal → no suggestion); **opinionated + concrete** (propose the specific fix with defaults chosen — the human approves **all / some / none**); **once per project** (one consolidated ask; respect "leave it"); **surface, never silently mutate** (color grades especially: propose and preview — a gray-world "correction" ruins an intentional sunset or neon look).

## Where to look — read only the file your task needs

| Task                                                                      | Read                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| resolve / reuse / adopt / ingest, flags, cascade, inventory               | `references/resolve.md`          |
| color grading, LUTs, smart grade (`--for`), grade-compare                 | `references/grading.md`          |
| voiceover / TTS, music, SFX, captions, transcription (audio engine)       | `references/audio.md`            |
| cut / reframe / transform existing media, exact error diffusion, HEVC     | `references/operations.md`       |
| source-aware creative treatments, realtime effects, overlays, reveals     | `references/media-treatments.md` |
| install + auth, provider table, RAM ladders, `--local-only`, `--provider` | `references/setup-providers.md`  |
| remembered preferences + frozen recipes (user memory)                     | `references/memory.md`           |
| ownership matrix, usage stats, telemetry, privacy (maintainer-facing)     | `references/meta.md`             |

candidate and inspect one after-sheet for ordinary correction or polish.
Escalate to individual frames or moving draft evidence only when the result is
ambiguous, temporal, stylized, LUT-based, HDR/LOG-sensitive, private, or
brand-critical.

For ordinary correction or polish, persist the final treatment's
preset/adjustment JSON.
Do not generate a `.cube` LUT merely to encode exposure, shadows, contrast, or
warmth. Use a LUT only when the user supplies one or the selected treatment
explicitly owns one. `resolve --type grade --for ... --analyze` is measurement
evidence, not permission to replace the chosen treatment with a generated LUT.
Do not recreate supported vignette, grain, blur, pixelate, color, or treatment
effects with CSS/SVG overlays; that bypasses Studio controls and the canonical
preview/render shader path.

## Be proactive — run a media opportunity pass

The human usually can't tell which media would lift the piece. You can. When you build or review a composition, do **one** grounded scan and then **ask once** — don't silently add, and don't nag per asset.

Surface an opportunity only when a concrete signal is present:

| Signal detected                                          | Offer                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| On-screen text / a script with no voiceover              | TTS voiceover (audio engine)                                                                           |
| Emoji or a `<div>` styled as an icon                     | resolve real `icon`s                                                                                   |
| Image that is a placeholder, tiny, or upscaled-looking   | a better `image` (and/or upscale — see `references/operations.md`)                                     |
| Hard scene cuts / transitions with no sound              | transition `sfx`                                                                                       |
| A piece over ~10s with no music bed                      | `bgm`                                                                                                  |
| Footage that reads under/over-exposed or color-cast      | a corrective grade (inspect it with `hyperframes media-treatment --selector '#hero' --analyze --json`) |
| Photographic media that feels visually flat or off-topic | one specific source-appropriate preset or custom treatment, with the intended target named             |
| A meaningful media entrance/reveal that feels static     | one supported seek-safe treatment animation; preserve color unless the request also justifies a preset |

Rules that keep this a help, not nagware: **grounded, not generic** (no signal → no suggestion); **opinionated + concrete** (propose the specific fix with defaults chosen — the human approves **all / some / none**); **once per project** (one consolidated ask; respect "leave it"); **surface, never silently mutate** (color grades especially: propose and preview — a gray-world "correction" ruins an intentional sunset or neon look).

## Where to look — read only the file your task needs

| Task                                                                      | Read                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| resolve / reuse / adopt / ingest, flags, cascade, inventory               | `references/resolve.md`          |
| color grading, LUTs, smart grade (`--for`), grade-compare                 | `references/grading.md`          |
| voiceover / TTS, music, SFX, captions, transcription (audio engine)       | `references/audio.md`            |
| cut / reframe / transform existing media, exact error diffusion, HEVC     | `references/operations.md`       |
| source-aware creative treatments, realtime effects, overlays, reveals     | `references/media-treatments.md` |
| install + auth, provider table, RAM ladders, `--local-only`, `--provider` | `references/setup-providers.md`  |
| remembered preferences + frozen recipes (user memory)                     | `references/memory.md`           |
| ownership matrix, usage stats, telemetry, privacy (maintainer-facing)     | `references/meta.md`             |

### rockwood-edit/audio/make_audio.py  (8,110 octets)
==============================================================================
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rockwood Method edit — original music bed + sound design, 100 % synthesized (no samples, no licensing).
Outputs music.wav / sfx.wav (27.6 s, 44.1 kHz stereo). SFX are placed at the exact times of the on-screen events
(EVENTS below, shared with build.py through events.json)."""
import json
import numpy as np
from scipy import signal
from scipy.io import wavfile

SR = 44100
DUR = 27.6
N = int(SR * DUR)
rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
BPM = 92
BEAT = 60 / BPM


def lp(x, fc, order=2):
    b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), "low"); return signal.lfilter(b, a, x)


def hp(x, fc, order=2):
    b, a = signal.butter(order, fc / (SR / 2), "high"); return signal.lfilter(b, a, x)


def bp(x, f1, f2, order=2):
    b, a = signal.butter(order, [f1 / (SR / 2), f2 / (SR / 2)], "band"); return signal.lfilter(b, a, x)


def env_exp(n, tau):
    return np.exp(-np.arange(n) / (SR * tau))


def put(buf, t, x, g=1.0):
    i = int(t * SR)
    if i < 0 or i >= buf.shape[-1]:
        return
    j = min(buf.shape[-1], i + x.shape[-1])
    buf[..., i:j] += x[..., : j - i] * g


def midi(m):
    return 440 * 2 ** ((m - 69) / 12)


# ───────────────────────── MUSIC ─────────────────────────
M = np.zeros((2, N))
# progression (one chord per 2 bars): Dmaj7 · Bm7 · Gmaj7 · A6   (warm, optimistic)
CH = [
    ([50, 57, 61, 66], 38),  # Dmaj7 (D F# A C#)  bass D
    ([47, 54, 57, 62], 35),  # Bm7
    ([43, 50, 54, 59], 31),  # Gmaj7
    ([45, 52, 57, 61], 33),  # A
]
BAR = 4 * BEAT
nbars = int(DUR / BAR) + 2


def pad(notes, dur):
    n = int(dur * SR); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    out = np.zeros((2, n))
    for k, m in enumerate(notes):
        for det, pan in ((-0.07, -0.5), (0.07, 0.5), (0.0, 0.0)):
            f = midi(m + 12) * 2 ** (det / 12)
            s = signal.sawtooth(2 * np.pi * f * t) * 0.5 + np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) * 0.5
            gl = np.cos((pan + 1) * np.pi / 4); gr = np.sin((pan + 1) * np.pi / 4)
            out[0] += s * gl; out[1] += s * gr
    out = lp(out, 1500, 2) * 0.05
    e = np.minimum(1, t / 0.5) * np.minimum(1, (dur - t) / 0.7)
    return out * e


def pluck(m, dur=0.5):
    n = int(dur * SR); t = np.arange(n) / SR; f = midi(m)
    s = signal.sawtooth(2 * np.pi * f * t) * 0.35 + np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * 2 * t) * 0.15 + np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) * 0.5
    return lp(s, 3200, 2) * env_exp(n, 0.14)


def bassnote(m, dur):
    n = int(dur * SR); t = np.arange(n) / SR; f = midi(m)
    s = np.sin(2 * np.pi * f * t) + 0.25 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 2 * f * t)
    return s * np.minimum(1, t / 0.01) * env_exp(n, 0.5) * 0.28


def kick():
    n = int(0.3 * SR); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 48 + 90 * np.exp(-t * 28)
    ph = 2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR
    return np.sin(ph) * env_exp(n, 0.1) * 0.55


def hat():
    n = int(0.06 * SR)
    return hp(rng.standard_normal(n), 7000) * env_exp(n, 0.012) * 0.12


for b in range(nbars):
    t0 = b * BAR
    notes, root = CH[(b // 2) % 4]
    if b % 2 == 0:
        p = pad(notes, BAR * 2 + 0.3)
        put(M, t0, p)
    # bass: root on 1, pickup on "and of 2"
    bn = bassnote(root, BEAT * 1.5)
    put(M[0], t0, bn); put(M[1], t0, bn)
    bn2 = bassnote(root + (7 if b % 2 else 0), BEAT)
    put(M[0], t0 + BEAT * 2.5, bn2, 0.8); put(M[1], t0 + BEAT * 2.5, bn2, 0.8)
    # soft kick on 1 and 3
    for beat in (0, 2):
        k = kick(); put(M[0], t0 + beat * BEAT, k, 0.6); put(M[1], t0 + beat * BEAT, k, 0.6)
    # offbeat hats
    for i in range(8):
        if i % 2 == 1:
            h = hat(); pan = 0.3 if (i // 2) % 2 else -0.3
            put(M[0], t0 + i * BEAT / 2, h, 0.5 + pan * 0.3); put(M[1], t0 + i * BEAT / 2, h, 0.5 - pan * 0.3)
    # 8th-note pluck arpeggio (from bar 2 for a build)
    if b >= 2:
        arp = [notes[0] + 12, notes[2] + 12, notes[3] + 12, notes[2] + 12, notes[1] + 12, notes[2] + 12, notes[3] + 12, notes[2] + 12]
        for i, m in enumerate(arp):
            if i % 2 == 0 or b >= 4:
                pl = pluck(m + 12 if i % 3 == 0 else m)
                pan = -0.35 if i % 2 else 0.35
                put(M[0], t0 + i * BEAT / 2, pl, 0.15 * (1 - pan * 0.5)); put(M[1], t0 + i * BEAT / 2, pl, 0.15 * (1 + pan * 0.5))

# simple stereo reverb (decaying noise convolution)
irn = int(1.4 * SR)
ir = [lp(rng.standard_normal(irn), 4000) * env_exp(irn, 0.35) for _ in range(2)]
wet = np.stack([signal.fftconvolve(M[c], ir[c])[:N] for c in range(2)])
M = M + wet * 0.018
# fades + master
t = np.arange(N) / SR
M *= np.minimum(1, t / 1.2) * np.minimum(1, (DUR - t) / 1.4)
M *= 0.9 / max(1e-9, np.abs(M).max())

# ───────────────────────── SFX ─────────────────────────
EV = json.load(open("/home/user/rockwood-edit/audio/events.json"))
S = np.zeros((2, N))


def whoosh(dur=0.5, up=True, g=0.5):
    n = int(dur * SR); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = rng.standard_normal(n)
    fc = (400 + 5200 * (t / dur) ** 2) if up else (5600 - 5000 * (t / dur))
    out = np.zeros(n); blk = 512
    y = np.zeros(n)
    for i in range(0, n, blk):
        f = float(np.clip(fc[min(i, n - 1)], 150, 9000))
        b, a = signal.butter(2, [max(80, f * 0.6) / (SR / 2), min(f * 1.4, 10000) / (SR / 2)], "band")
        seg = signal.lfilter(b, a, x[i:i + blk * 2])[:blk]
        y[i:i + len(seg)] = seg[: n - i]
    e = np.sin(np.pi * np.clip(t / dur, 0, 1)) ** 1.5
    return y * e * g


def pop(g=0.5, f0=620):
    n = int(0.16 * SR); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = f0 + 700 * np.exp(-t * 40)
    ph = 2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR
    return (np.sin(ph) * env_exp(n, 0.05) + 0.4 * np.sin(2 * ph) * env_exp(n, 0.02)) * g


def thump(g=0.7):
    n = int(0.45 * SR); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    f = 38 + 80 * np.exp(-t * 22)
    ph = 2 * np.pi * np.cumsum(f) / SR
    return np.sin(ph) * env_exp(n, 0.14) * g


def riser(dur, g=0.35):
    n = int(dur * SR); t = np.arange(n) / SR
    x = rng.standard_normal(n)
    fc = 300 + 6500 * (t / dur) ** 2.2
    y = np.zeros(n); blk = 512
    for i in range(0, n, blk):
        f = float(fc[min(i, n - 1)])
        b, a = signal.butter(2, [f * 0.5 / (SR / 2), min(f * 1.6, 12000) / (SR / 2)], "band")
        seg = signal.lfilter(b, a, x[i:i + blk * 2])[:blk]
        y[i:i + len(seg)] = seg[: n - i]
    return y * (t / dur) ** 1.8 * g


def tick(g=0.18):
    n = int(0.03 * SR)
    return hp(rng.standard_normal(n), 3000) * env_exp(n, 0.006) * g


def stereo(x, t0, g=1.0, pan=0.0):
    put(S[0], t0, x, g * np.cos((pan + 1) * np.pi / 4) * 1.41)
    put(S[1], t0, x, g * np.sin((pan + 1) * np.pi / 4) * 1.41)


for ev in EV:
    t0, kind = ev["t"], ev["k"]
    if kind == "cut":      # jump-cut punch-in: low thump + short whoosh
        stereo(thump(0.5), t0, 1.0); stereo(whoosh(0.28, False, 0.28), max(0, t0 - 0.06), 1.0)
    elif kind == "whoosh":
        stereo(whoosh(0.5, True, 0.5), max(0, t0 - 0.22), 1.0, ev.get("pan", 0))
    elif kind == "pop":
        stereo(pop(0.42, ev.get("f", 620)), t0, 1.0, ev.get("pan", 0))
    elif kind == "swish":
        stereo(whoosh(0.32, True, 0.38), max(0, t0 - 0.14), 1.0, ev.get("pan", 0)); stereo(pop(0.28, 520), t0 + 0.04, 1.0)
    elif kind == "stamp":
        stereo(np.pad(thump(0.9), (0, int(0.7 * SR))) + lp(rng.standard_normal(int(1.15 * SR)), 2200) * env_exp(int(1.15 * SR), 0.18) * 0.35, t0, 1.0)
    elif kind == "riser":
        stereo(riser(ev["d"], 0.5), t0, 1.0)
    elif kind == "hit":
        stereo(np.pad(thump(1.0), (0, int(0.7 * SR))) + lp(rng.standard_normal(int(1.15 * SR)), 3000) * env_exp(int(1.15 * SR), 0.3) * 0.45, t0, 1.0)
        stereo(pop(0.35, 880), t0 + 0.02, 1.0)
    elif kind == "ticks":
        for i in range(ev["n"]):
            stereo(tick(0.22), t0 + i * ev["gap"], 1.0)

S *= 0.9 / max(1e-9, np.abs(S).max())


def save(name, x):
    y = (np.clip(x.T, -1, 1) * 32767).astype(np.int16)
    wavfile.write(name, SR, y)


save("/home/user/rockwood-edit/audio/music.wav", M)
save("/home/user/rockwood-edit/audio/sfx.wav", S)
print("ok", M.shape, S.shape)

### .agents/skills/hyperframes/SKILL.md  (17,943 octets)
